entities.summary: Sadīd ud-Dīn Muhammad Ibn Muhammad 'Aufī Bukhārī, also known under the laqab Nour ud-Dīn, was a Persian historian, philologist, and author. Born in Bukhara, Fergana Valley of Central Asia, around 1180, he was a renowned scholar and collector of traditional Islamic knowledge. His magnum opus, 'Asād al-Muṣaḥabah' (The Book of the Converse), is a seminal work on Islamic theology, jurisprudence, and Hadith scholarship. Nour ud-Dīn's work had a profound impact on the development of Islamic scholarship in the Middle East and Central Asia, shaping the intellectual trajectory of the region for centuries to come. His writings on the Hadith tradition, in particular, remain a cornerstone of Islamic scholarship to this day. Through his tireless efforts to preserve and transmit Islamic knowledge, Nour ud-Dīn played a pivotal role in the transmission of Islamic learning from the Middle East to other parts of the world, leaving an indelible mark on the intellectual landscape of the Islamic Golden Age.
